jobs.title: Associate Director of Development, University Advancement
jobs.description:
Job Overview

The Associate Director of Development plays a critical role in advancing the University’s fundraising priorities by strategically managing a comprehensive donor pipeline. This position is responsible for the full lifecycle of donor engagement including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities. It requires exceptional time management and organizational skills to effectively prioritize and move prospects through each stage while maintaining momentum across a diverse portfolio. Success in this role depends on strong communication abilities to clearly articulate the University’s mission and impact while building trust and meaningful relationships with a broad range of constituents.

A key focus of the position is frontline fundraising with a special focus on gifts requiring demonstrated success across both annual giving and major giving, in the $5k-$25k+ range. The Associate Director applies strategic thinking to assess donor readiness, align opportunities with institutional priorities, and move prospects thoughtfully from initial engagement to major gift consideration. This work is grounded in a disciplined approach to planning and execution, supported by a strong work ethic and a commitment to achieving measurable results that contribute to divisional and university wide fundraising goals.

The role also emphasizes the use of data informed strategies to guide decision making and portfolio management. By analyzing donor trends, engagement metrics, and giving patterns, the Associate Director develops targeted approaches that enhance effectiveness and maximize philanthropic outcomes. This analytical mindset, combined with sound judgment and adaptability, ensures that efforts remain focused, efficient, and aligned with evolving institutional needs.

Collaboration is central to the success of this position, as the Associate Director works closely with internal partners and external stakeholders to maximize philanthropic opportunities. The ability to effectively engage, influence, and coordinate with colleagues, donors, and community members is essential to building a strong culture of philanthropy. Through these efforts, the Associate Director advances the University’s mission and upholds its commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and access, fostering an environment where philanthropy supports broad and meaningful institutional impact.

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

The Career Development Center is seeking an Executive Director
of Career Development

The Executive Director of Career Development provides university-wide leadership for career development at Oregon State University, advancing a comprehensive, coordinated and student-centered career ecosystem that serves undergraduate and graduate students across Corvallis, OSU-Cascades in Bend, and Ecampus. The Executive Director leads the strategy, programs, partnerships, operations and assessment efforts that help students explore purpose, build career readiness and advancement, connect academic learning to future pathways, engage with employers and alumni, and transition successfully to meaningful work, graduate education, service, entrepreneurship and other post-graduation opportunities.

This position is responsible for building upon Oregon State University’s ecosystem of career development and the vision of Beyond OSU: a university-wide commitment to integrating career development across the student experience so that every student has access to timely, relevant and inclusive career learning, experiences and connections. The Executive Director works collaboratively across the institution, including academic colleges, Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, OSU-Cascades, Ecampus, graduate education, advising, experiential learning, alumni engagement, employer relations, industry partnerships, student employment/University Human Resources, faculty and staff networks, and other university partners to strengthen career readiness as a shared institutional priority.

The Executive Director provides strategic leadership for the Career Development Center and related career development initiatives, including career education, career integration, employer and alumni engagement, experiential learning, technology, data, assessment, staff development, resource stewardship, and university-wide partnerships. This role develops and evaluates short- and long-range plans, sets standards for high-quality and equitable career development practices, and leads efforts to ensure that career development is intentionally embedded within curricular and co-curricular experiences for students across modalities, campuses and academic levels.

The Executive Director reports to the Associate Vice President of Student Affairs and serves as a member of the Associate Vice President’s leadership team. jobs.title: Executive Director of Academic and Career Engagement
jobs.description:
General Summary:

The primary mission of the Academic and Career Engagement and Success (ACES) Center is to provide holistic, high-quality, and culturally responsive academic and career success advising, programming, and experiential learning. The department values inclusive excellence through holistic student success and equitable outcomes.

The Executive Director of Academic and Career Engagement provides advanced strategic leadership and vision for the university’s comprehensive academic and career development services function. This role oversees the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of comprehensive academic and career-related services, programs, and initiatives for students and alumni across all academic disciplines, while ensuring operational excellence, inclusive practice, and data-informed decision-making.

The Executive Director leads division-wide strategy execution, including the development and implementation of a cohesive career communities model, institutional experiential learning frameworks, and expanded employer and industry partnerships. Serving as a key strategic advisor to the AVP and campus leadership, they will work collaboratively with faculty, staff, administrators, and external stakeholders to foster comprehensive academic and career exploration, career readiness, employment opportunities, and post-graduation success. The position includes the development and oversight of a cohesive career communities model, enhancement of strategic employer partnerships, and collaboration to establish a campus-wide comprehensive experiential learning model that supports student success and retention.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice Provost (AVP), the Executive Director oversees and integrates multiple functional areas including comprehensive academic and career advising services, employer engagement, career communities, and departmental operations including supervision, training, program assessment, and creative leadership. They will oversee daily operations leading a team of academic and career advisors and in collaboration with the Assistant Director of Programming, Assistant Director of Employer Partnerships, and Assistant Director of Career Development and Education related to academic and career advising, career development via career communities, strategic employer partnerships, signature events, experiential learning within ACES and across campus, and assessment of service delivery and outcomes.

Examples of Duties:

Strategic Leadership & Planning:

Under the direction of the AVP and in collaboration with the leadership team align comprehensive academic and career development and education, experiential learning, career communities, and employer engagement models with institutional goals.
Lead and assess short- and long-term strategic planning efforts for comprehensive academic and career services and experiential learning initiatives, including the development of measurable goals and key performance indicators.
Contribute at a senior level to budget planning, resource allocation, and operational decision-making, beyond day-to-day operations and program management.
Translate institutional strategy into scalable programs and services within ACES and across career communities.
Partner with the AVP in strengthening strategic external partnerships toward advancing comprehensive academic and career services on the campus.

Career Services Program Management:

Provide senior-level oversight of comprehensive academic and career services, including academic and career advising, graduate and alumni career engagement, career communities, experiential learning programs, and employer partnerships.
Oversee the planning and delivery of career fairs, employer recruitment activities, workshops and seminars, networking events, and job and internship placement aimed at enhancing students’ career readiness.
In collaboration with the AVP, provide leadership-level guidance, consultation, supervision, and training for Academic and Career Advisors who provide career development services to students.
Ensure that career development services are accessible to students across all disciplines and academic levels.
Advance and scale student participation in the experiential learning programs and career readiness pathways.
Collaborate with campus leaders to expand and coordinate experiential learning programs across campus to align with career and learning communities.

Team Leadership & Development:

Provide high-level supervision and mentorship to a team of academic and career services professionals, fostering a collaborative, inclusive work culture, and high-performing work environment.
Lead staff recruitment, training, evaluation, and professional development initiatives aligned with industry standards and competencies to effectively support comprehensive academic and career services within a career communities model.
Establish expectations for innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the team.
Provide regular feedback, coaching, and performance management.

Employer Relations & Partnerships:

Develop and implement a comprehensive employer engagement strategy that strengthens partnerships with regional, national, and global organizations, incorporating industry advisory board structures, aligned with the strategic vision of ACES and the campus.
Lead efforts to expand internship pipelines, experiential learning placements, and employment outcomes for students and alumni.
Implement robust on-campus recruiting strategies and employer-facing programming.
Expand and strengthen partnerships with industry leaders.

Assessment & Reporting:

Lead assessment strategy to evaluate the effectiveness and impact of comprehensive academic and career services, including career outcomes, employer satisfaction, and student engagement.
Collaborate with the AVP to align assessment practices with divisional and institutional reporting needs, including tracking data on student usage, learning outcomes, retention and graduation rates, first destination data, and employment and workforce trends for UMass Boston graduates and alumni.
Regularly report on program successes, challenges, and improvements to senior leadership and other stakeholders.
Use data proactively to inform strategic decisions and program refinement in operations and management of comprehensive academic and career advising services and experiential learning programs.

Student and Alumni Engagement:

Provide advanced career coaching and guidance for students and alumni, including career exploration, resume development, job search strategies, interview preparation, and professional networking.
Design and oversee initiatives to foster sustained alumni engagement with career services, mentoring, and employer connections, fostering a lifelong connection to the university.

Collaboration with Campus Stakeholders:

Partner with faculty and academic departments to embed career readiness and experiential learning into curricula and co-curricular experiences to ensure comprehensive career services are an integral part of students' academic journey.
Collaborate with key stakeholders across campus to align comprehensive academic and career initiatives within ACES services with broader student success and retention strategies.
Advise academic and administrative leaders on workforce and employment trends toward meeting the specialized needs of students in each of the colleges, aligning with career communities, and advancing the general education capabilities.

Additional Responsibilities

Represent the university in professional associations and external partnerships related to comprehensive academic and career services and workforce development.
Perform other duties as assigned.

The incumbent will be required to work nights and weekends, as needed. Some travel may be required.

Proven ability to influence and collaborate with faculty, senior administrators, and external partners.
Data-informed approach to strategic planning and evaluation, with experience in using assessment tools and data to improve programs.
Active engagement with professional associations (e.g., NACE, EACE, NACADA).
Exceptional knowledge of comprehensive academic and career advising techniques, employment trends, labor market analysis, and employer needs.
Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, and communication skills.
Ability to develop and implement innovative programs and services that meet the needs of a diverse student body.
Exceptional networking, partnership-building, and relationship-management skills.
Exceptional knowledge of career management platforms and innovative technology used in career services.
Proven track record of working with diverse student populations and employers from various industries.
Demonstrated ability to develop strategic partnerships and to oversee major projects from development to implementation.

jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer

Multi-Location Dermatology & Aesthetics Practice

Atlanta, GA — four locations

Our Mission
We provide our families with compassionate skin care and medical education, giving them the comfort and confidence to live healthy and beautiful lives. We put our patients first, work to constantly improve our patients' experience, and demand excellence from our entire team.

Our Vision
Everyone deserves healthy skin.

Our Values
• Patient-focused
• Team-focused
• Community-focused

The Opportunity
The Chief Operating Officer is the senior-most administrative executive in the organization, reporting directly to the two physician Owners. The COO is accountable for the operational and financial performance of all four clinics and the aesthetics division, leads the practice's management team, and partners with the Owners on strategic planning, growth, and major business decisions. The COO carries direct accountability for revenue growth and EBITDA performance across the practice.
The COO is expected to lead through the management team and hold vendors accountable rather than absorb work personally, and to build an operating structure that does not depend on any single person. The practice operates without a CEO layer, which means real authority, exposure, and a short line to decisions.
The right candidate is someone energized by building operating discipline, developing managers into stronger leaders, and bringing clarity to a growing organization that has significant room to execute.

Key Responsibilities
Executive and Strategic Leadership
• Partner with the physician Owners on strategic planning, growth initiatives, service line expansion, and major capital and business decisions
• Translate ownership objectives into annual operating plans with named owners, deadlines, and measurable outcomes
• Serve as the point of resolution for cross-departmental priorities, escalations, and resource decisions
• Return the Owners' time to clinical care and strategic direction by taking genuine ownership of operations

Financial Leadership
• Own the operating budget, forecast, and expense discipline across all locations and the aesthetics division
• Drive EBITDA growth and margin improvement, with accountability for both revenue performance and the cost structure that supports it
• Establish a disciplined monthly close and financial review rhythm, working with the practice's accounting resources and external CPA firm
• Help define and build out the internal finance function, then lead through it
• Deliver location-level profit and loss visibility, including appropriate separation of administrative overhead from operating locations
• Monitor and improve revenue cycle performance in collaboration with the Billing Manager
• Own payer relationships and lead the renegotiation of managed care contracts, including reimbursement terms for advanced practice providers
• Understand expense and payroll growth at the line-item level and hold cost growth in a defensible relationship to revenue growth
• Oversee payroll, compensation structure, and performance-based incentive programs

Operations and Team Leadership
• Lead a management team spanning HR, finance, billing, call center, Mohs, dermatopathology, aesthetics, and site management across four locations
• Oversee the recently launched dermatopathology service line and lead the development of an in-house laboratory
• Chair the weekly management team meeting and maintain a consistent one-on-one cadence with all direct reports
• Maintain regular on-site presence across locations to ensure consistent standards, staffing, and patient experience
• Coordinate provider schedules across sites to maximize patient access
• Build and maintain an operating dashboard covering access, provider productivity, revenue cycle, patient experience, staffing and turnover, aesthetics performance, and progress against strategic initiatives

Aesthetics Division
• Own the operational and financial performance of the aesthetics division, including service and product mix, pricing, provider productivity, inventory, and reconciliation
• Bring or develop genuine commercial depth in aesthetics as a growth line rather than as an adjunct to medical dermatology

People and Culture
• Direct hiring, performance review cycles, and personnel decisions in partnership with HR
• Manage the PEO relationship, including annual benefits selection and renewal
• Develop managers into stronger leaders through coaching, clear expectations, and accountability
• Build staffing pipelines for clinical and administrative roles, with candidate pools for high-turnover positions and succession plans for key roles, so vacancies are filled from a bench rather than from a standing start
• Own retention as a measured outcome, particularly in clinical support roles

Vendors, Technology and Facilities
• Own vendor selection, contract review and negotiation, and renewal management across IT, marketing, telecommunications, software, and clinical supply
• Oversee the managed IT services relationship and the practice management and EMR platform. This role directs and holds vendors accountable; it does not perform hands-on technical work
• Manage facilities and lease matters, including negotiations, amendments, and tenant improvement projects, with an eye toward potential practice acquisition of current or future office space
• Oversee inventory and procurement systems across all sites

Compliance and Clinical Operations Support
• Coordinate with the Compliance Officer to maintain regulatory readiness across all locations
• Build the operational infrastructure for new clinical service lines as the practice expands
• Support clinical leadership on provider workflow, capacity, and coverage planning

How This Role Works
The practice uses the Working Genius framework to understand how people contribute and where they thrive. We are being direct about the working style this role requires, because fit matters here as much as the resume.

Candidates advancing in the process will be invited to complete a Working Genius assessment. There is no single correct result. It is used to have an honest conversation about fit and about how the role and the surrounding team work best together.

This role will suit someone who is energized by:
• Exercising judgment.
• Supporting and developing other people.
• Rallying people to action.
• Finishing things.
• Delegating deliberately.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months
• A documented responsibility map is in place, with work positioned where it belongs rather than concentrated by default
• The management team operates with clear expectations, a consistent cadence, and defined decision rights
• Monthly financial close and review run on a predictable rhythm, with location-level reporting the Owners trust
• Expense and payroll growth are understood at the line-item level and managed against plan
• EBITDA is measured and reported with a clear improvement plan agreed with the Owners
• Managed care contracts have been reviewed and a renegotiation plan is underway
• Provider schedules stay full and patient access improves across all four locations
• The aesthetics division has clear performance measures and reconciliation that closes on time
• Vendor contracts and renewals are actively managed with no unplanned auto-renewals or lapses
• Retention in clinical support roles is measured, understood, and improving
• The Owners spend their time on clinical care and strategic direction, not daily operations

Qualifications
• Minimum 5 years of progressive operations leadership in multi-site healthcare, with direct profit and loss accountability
• Demonstrated success leading managers across multiple locations and functions
• Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and financial reporting, with the ability to interrogate the numbers and hold the finance function to account
• Demonstrated track record of improving EBITDA or operating margin across a multi-site organization
• Experience negotiating and executing vendor contracts, leases, and service agreements
• Working fluency across HR, IT, compliance, and facilities functions, sufficient to direct specialists and vendors
• EMR or practice management platform experience; ModMed (EMA) preferred
• A self-starter who can identify issues, exercise sound judgment, and take initiative
• Master’s degree preferred; qualified candidates without one are encouraged to apply
• Dermatology, aesthetics, or specialty physician practice experience strongly preferred
• Experience in physician-owned private practice, particularly reporting directly to owners without a CEO layer, preferred
• Experience building or maturing a finance and reporting function, rather than only inheriting one, preferred
• Commercial experience in aesthetics, medical spa, or retail-adjacent healthcare services preferred
• Experience negotiating or renegotiating managed care and payer contracts preferred
• Experience with commercial lease negotiation or property acquisition preferred
• Experience launching or scaling ancillary service lines, such as pathology or laboratory services, preferred

Compensation and Work Environment
• Base salary starting at $200,000, commensurate with experience, with a performance-based incentive component
• Full-time and on-site
• Benefits provided through the practice's PEO
• Physician-owned and independent, with no private equity involvement

Apply for This Position

All inquiries will be held in strict confidence, the identity of the practice will be shared with candidates at the appropriate stage of the process.

Chief Operating Officer

Multi-Location Dermatology & Aesthetics Practice

Atlanta, GA — four locations

Our Mission
We provide our families with compassionate skin care and medical education, giving them the comfort and confidence to live healthy and beautiful lives. We put our patients first, work to constantly improve our patients' experience, and demand excellence from our entire team.

Our Vision
Everyone deserves healthy skin.

Our Values
• Patient-focused
• Team-focused
• Community-focused

The Opportunity
The Chief Operating Officer is the senior-most administrative executive in the organization, reporting directly to the two physician Owners. The COO is accountable for the operational and financial performance of all four clinics and the aesthetics division, leads the practice's management team, and partners with the Owners on strategic planning, growth, and major business decisions. The COO carries direct accountability for revenue growth and EBITDA performance across the practice.
The COO is expected to lead through the management team and hold vendors accountable rather than absorb work personally, and to build an operating structure that does not depend on any single person. The practice operates without a CEO layer, which means real authority, exposure, and a short line to decisions.
The right candidate is someone energized by building operating discipline, developing managers into stronger leaders, and bringing clarity to a growing organization that has significant room to execute.

Key Responsibilities
Executive and Strategic Leadership
• Partner with the physician Owners on strategic planning, growth initiatives, service line expansion, and major capital and business decisions
• Translate ownership objectives into annual operating plans with named owners, deadlines, and measurable outcomes
• Serve as the point of resolution for cross-departmental priorities, escalations, and resource decisions
• Return the Owners' time to clinical care and strategic direction by taking genuine ownership of operations

Financial Leadership
• Own the operating budget, forecast, and expense discipline across all locations and the aesthetics division
• Drive EBITDA growth and margin improvement, with accountability for both revenue performance and the cost structure that supports it
• Establish a disciplined monthly close and financial review rhythm, working with the practice's accounting resources and external CPA firm
• Help define and build out the internal finance function, then lead through it
• Deliver location-level profit and loss visibility, including appropriate separation of administrative overhead from operating locations
• Monitor and improve revenue cycle performance in collaboration with the Billing Manager
• Own payer relationships and lead the renegotiation of managed care contracts, including reimbursement terms for advanced practice providers
• Understand expense and payroll growth at the line-item level and hold cost growth in a defensible relationship to revenue growth
• Oversee payroll, compensation structure, and performance-based incentive programs

Operations and Team Leadership
• Lead a management team spanning HR, finance, billing, call center, Mohs, dermatopathology, aesthetics, and site management across four locations
• Oversee the recently launched dermatopathology service line and lead the development of an in-house laboratory
• Chair the weekly management team meeting and maintain a consistent one-on-one cadence with all direct reports
• Maintain regular on-site presence across locations to ensure consistent standards, staffing, and patient experience
• Coordinate provider schedules across sites to maximize patient access
• Build and maintain an operating dashboard covering access, provider productivity, revenue cycle, patient experience, staffing and turnover, aesthetics performance, and progress against strategic initiatives

Aesthetics Division
• Own the operational and financial performance of the aesthetics division, including service and product mix, pricing, provider productivity, inventory, and reconciliation
• Bring or develop genuine commercial depth in aesthetics as a growth line rather than as an adjunct to medical dermatology

People and Culture
• Direct hiring, performance review cycles, and personnel decisions in partnership with HR
• Manage the PEO relationship, including annual benefits selection and renewal
• Develop managers into stronger leaders through coaching, clear expectations, and accountability
• Build staffing pipelines for clinical and administrative roles, with candidate pools for high-turnover positions and succession plans for key roles, so vacancies are filled from a bench rather than from a standing start
• Own retention as a measured outcome, particularly in clinical support roles

Vendors, Technology and Facilities
• Own vendor selection, contract review and negotiation, and renewal management across IT, marketing, telecommunications, software, and clinical supply
• Oversee the managed IT services relationship and the practice management and EMR platform. This role directs and holds vendors accountable; it does not perform hands-on technical work
• Manage facilities and lease matters, including negotiations, amendments, and tenant improvement projects, with an eye toward potential practice acquisition of current or future office space
• Oversee inventory and procurement systems across all sites

Compliance and Clinical Operations Support
• Coordinate with the Compliance Officer to maintain regulatory readiness across all locations
• Build the operational infrastructure for new clinical service lines as the practice expands
• Support clinical leadership on provider workflow, capacity, and coverage planning

How This Role Works
The practice uses the Working Genius framework to understand how people contribute and where they thrive. We are being direct about the working style this role requires, because fit matters here as much as the resume.

Candidates advancing in the process will be invited to complete a Working Genius assessment. There is no single correct result. It is used to have an honest conversation about fit and about how the role and the surrounding team work best together.

This role will suit someone who is energized by:
• Exercising judgment.
• Supporting and developing other people.
• Rallying people to action.
• Finishing things.
• Delegating deliberately.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months
• A documented responsibility map is in place, with work positioned where it belongs rather than concentrated by default
• The management team operates with clear expectations, a consistent cadence, and defined decision rights
• Monthly financial close and review run on a predictable rhythm, with location-level reporting the Owners trust
• Expense and payroll growth are understood at the line-item level and managed against plan
• EBITDA is measured and reported with a clear improvement plan agreed with the Owners
• Managed care contracts have been reviewed and a renegotiation plan is underway
• Provider schedules stay full and patient access improves across all four locations
• The aesthetics division has clear performance measures and reconciliation that closes on time
• Vendor contracts and renewals are actively managed with no unplanned auto-renewals or lapses
• Retention in clinical support roles is measured, understood, and improving
• The Owners spend their time on clinical care and strategic direction, not daily operations

Qualifications
• Minimum 5 years of progressive operations leadership in multi-site healthcare, with direct profit and loss accountability
• Demonstrated success leading managers across multiple locations and functions
• Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and financial reporting, with the ability to interrogate the numbers and hold the finance function to account
• Demonstrated track record of improving EBITDA or operating margin across a multi-site organization
• Experience negotiating and executing vendor contracts, leases, and service agreements
• Working fluency across HR, IT, compliance, and facilities functions, sufficient to direct specialists and vendors
• EMR or practice management platform experience; ModMed (EMA) preferred
• A self-starter who can identify issues, exercise sound judgment, and take initiative
• Master’s degree preferred; qualified candidates without one are encouraged to apply
• Dermatology, aesthetics, or specialty physician practice experience strongly preferred
• Experience in physician-owned private practice, particularly reporting directly to owners without a CEO layer, preferred
• Experience building or maturing a finance and reporting function, rather than only inheriting one, preferred
• Commercial experience in aesthetics, medical spa, or retail-adjacent healthcare services preferred
• Experience negotiating or renegotiating managed care and payer contracts preferred
• Experience with commercial lease negotiation or property acquisition preferred
• Experience launching or scaling ancillary service lines, such as pathology or laboratory services, preferred

Compensation and Work Environment
• Base salary starting at $200,000, commensurate with experience, with a performance-based incentive component
• Full-time and on-site
• Benefits provided through the practice's PEO
• Physician-owned and independent, with no private equity involvement
